geometry_edits.rationale: Wrap the dominant mass in a courtyard operation to produce a clearer public void and frontage response while preserving ancestry.
Increase the courtyard carve so the interior opening becomes a legible public space.
Open the court toward the verified access side to form an active street threshold.
Keep the ground organizer active so the court reads as usable neighborhood space rather than decorative subtraction.

graph_edits.rationale: Convert the split-wing macro into a clearer courtyard-based mass so the dominant form organizes around a usable public void rather than a generic split.
Enlarge the carved center to make the void legible as neighborhood public space.
Align the open side to the program access side so the verified frontage reads as an entry threshold rather than a sealed edge.
Keep a connecting element so the mass remains one coherent building rather than two disconnected fragments.
Strengthen the ground-level organizer to make the public threshold readable and continuous.

rationale: The candidate reads as a compact but unresolved split mass: in plan it suggests two blocks with a central notch/slot, yet across views the parts do not fully cohere into one dominant spatial rule. The parcel is respected, but the relationship to the verified frontage/access edge is weak; the blue edge is answered more by adjacency than by a clearly public seam, court, or entry threshold. The silhouette is not offensive as a staircase, but it is too generic and box-like to count as a resolved section for neighborhood living. Compared with the references, it has some similarity to courtyard-and-bridge neighborhood types, but it falls short on clarity of hierarchy, openness, and active ground response.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more pavilion-like and sculpturally open than the candidate; do not copy the curved roof language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise composition with a legible central void and bridging connector can support a neighborhood/public threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is a much larger multi-building complex; candidate should not emulate its scale or tower-like components.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like courtyard aggregation and stepped low-rise masses can organize public space while keeping hierarchy clear.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is cleaner and more articulated; candidate currently reads as a simple split box without a convincing public edge.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A rectangular mass with a carved central void and overhanging upper volume can create an active ground threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference is more horizontally expansive and integrated; candidate lacks that continuity and site responsiveness.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A low elongated mass with courtyard void and folded roof can produce a calm upper silhouette over an active base.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Reference has stronger connective hierarchy and a more explicit terrace section than the candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, interconnected wings around a shared open core can align mass, circulation, and public space.

warnings: Frontage/access response is underdeveloped for the verified road edge.
Massing appears coherent in some views but less convincing in section and opposite view; this risks a one-view-only understanding.
The form is too box-like and split without a clearly legible public void.
Do not treat the top chamfer as a meaningful roof/section strategy; it is not enough to satisfy program semantics.
